spec.sequence: From the road on the flat west of the pond the crown of the Hist shows over the trees on the crest, 40 m above the traveller. The road bends round the pond and the gate tower and the standing curtain hide the tree; the arch and the tower are what is seen. The road runs straight through the arch into the gate yard, holding its own bearing; the track then climbs the shoulder and the tree comes back on the left hand behind its ring of poles; at the top of the shoulder the bell kiosk shows ahead and the bay opens beyond it.
spec.wayfinding: Keep the pond on the left and hold the road's line through the arch to the lantern, then follow the track uphill with the pole ring on the left until the bell shows ahead.

spec.sequence: From a lighter at the roadstead the tall Pusbottom rooming house reads first above the mangrove, with the bell kiosk higher on the bench once the boat closes the channel. Along the channel the ridge block breaks the water on the right hand; then the pier head, the quay deck and the sheds along the lane come into view under the bluff.
spec.wayfinding: Steer left of the tall Pusbottom block, keep the ridge block to starboard and come alongside at the pier head; the deck is the end of the pier and the stair up to the bell leaves from the lane behind it.

spec.wayfinding: Follow the amber conduit up the face; it leads to the gate. Inside the gate the road runs straight to the foot of the great stair.

spec.sequence: From the shoulder at 240 m the watch column reads first, a thin stone thing against the void of the gorge with the grey crown of the Hist behind it; the ridge track drops behind the western rise and loses it; the frontage dais and the pen fence appear at the shelf head; then the shelf gate comes across the track, 15 m of timber with a walkway over the opening; through it the terrace runs east past the great stair head to the column at the lip.
spec.wayfinding: Follow the ridge track along the shoulder to the dais at the shelf head; the gate beyond it is the entrance. The terrace inside runs to the great stair and the column.

spec.fromDirection: south, up the authored poling channel from the Uxaneet water network
spec.sequence: From the water south of the ring the nine trunks stand above the reeds like the teeth of a comb, the elder trunk tallest among them; as the boat noses to the pier the bank's mangroves take them one by one; from the pier head the southern gap and wall read together above the bank; the landing path climbs north-west to the arch.
spec.wayfinding: From the pier, climb towards the gap in the trunks; the arch is round the trunk on the right.

spec.sequence: From the fork off the Archon-Gideon road the top of the elder trunk shows above the mangrove canopy, 31 m against 10 m at 116 m off; the track drops into low ground and the canopy closes over it for 60 m; at the pitch ground the whole ring rises as one grey wall of trunks and hut roofs; then the arch reads as the single gap in it, with the chime frame inside; through the arch the path runs straight to the round house.
spec.wayfinding: Keep the tallest trunk ahead; the arch is the single gap in the wall. The path through it runs to the round house.

spec.sequence: The Hist's crown stands over the jungle to the north-east from a bend away; the reeds hide the east bank until 20 m; the piles and the plank walk open up at the head of the creek; the bank above them is empty; the track that climbs from it is not seen until a boat is alongside.

spec.sequence: The road comes up out of the low ground to the west-north-west, climbing 21 m over its last 700. The Hist's crown stands above the canopy from 400 m out and holds until the line goes under closed cover. The pale trunk reads between the other trunks at about 30 m. The road skirts the camp's eastern flank and ends below it. The hut's door and the mule line are visible from the head of the camp track. The stair and the stage appear at its bend.
spec.wayfinding: Follow the worn line east and up out of the wet ground until the crown of the great tree stands overhead. The road ends below the camp. Take the track that leaves it northwards; it stops at the bottom of the stair.

spec.sequence: From the rise to the west the bare scarred crown of the north dead tree stands 8 m above the live canopy; the live trees between the rise and the knoll then hide the water as the ground climbs to 12 m; the stand's ramp comes into view head-on on the knoll top; from the deck the whole pan, the cairns, the platform and the cave mouth are seen at once; the stand path then drops past the dead willow and the cave mouth to the offering shelf.
spec.wayfinding: Walk east toward the bare crown; the ramp of the stand faces the walker on the knoll top. The path round the banks leaves from its foot.

spec.fromDirection: south-east, up the creek from the estuary, following the pole line
spec.sequence: The mouth pole shows first where the creek leaves the estuary; the poles then lead up the creek under a canopy of 0.93 while the water narrows to a boat's width and the pond stays out of sight; the head pole and the landing end the water; the bank path climbs west with the pond still hidden behind the slope; at the last bend the sky hole opens, the two dead cypresses show against it and then the water, with the lantern and the platform on its south shelf.
spec.wayfinding: Follow the poles up the creek to the landing, then the trodden path uphill toward the bare crowns; the offering bank is where the path meets the water again.

spec.value: The Xit-Xaht went on cutting stone after the Duskfall told every tribe to stop, on the order of a Hist they had bound with sap.
Tsono-Xuhil has not woken. The Amber Plasm seep has resumed and the conduits carry it up the escarpment into the works. The courses have started rising again.
Labour. Every course needs hands the tribe does not have, so the pens fill from the neighbouring villages; the shelf is also too small for what the shaper has drawn.

A firm rock shelf at the end of an upland ridge, 68 m by 42 m of buildable ground with the block face in its own southern lip. A headwater stream along that lip serves for mortar and slaking. The east side falls away in a 55 m escarpment that no neighbour climbs uninvited.
The conduits were cut, or another tribe accepted the invitation to help.

value.loreSource: UESP Lore:Xit-Xaht and Lore:Mazzatun (a tribe that raided neighbours for slave labour, under a Hist it bound); world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md section Mazzatun (stirring, building restarted); catalogue record place.dunmer-north.mazzatun (M3, few D3 builders, few taken labourers, one D4 shaper); docs/world/92-demographics.md
value.why: The Xit-Xaht who remain are a work gang and its shaper, about thirty in six households. They live underground in the halls behind the stair-throat, so the exterior carries no dwellings of theirs. The taken labourers, twelve to fifteen, are housed in three mud shells of 30 m2. The other twenty-three structures are the works: courses, stairs, kiln, scaffolds, block face, hoist, gate and conduit.

spec.value: A village grown where nine root-joined trunks stand in one ring; one tree by the Hist's reckoning, nine by the tribes' reckoning.
A tribe that hosts the convocation's overflow and has grown rich on it, renting pitch-rights to delegations that cannot fit at the Tsoko camp.
Hosting a province's delegations one month a year has made them arrogant the other eleven. Two neighbouring tribes now camp at Greenspring instead, on principle.

The ring of trunks encloses firm ground and makes its own stockade, with one gap left unbuilt for a gate. The knoll stands 4.8 m above the water table on firm lowland, with poleable water 32 m west and the Archon-Gideon road 160 m south-west.
A convocation held elsewhere would halve the village. The falling attendance the Root Talk ground counts publicly is already showing in their rents.

value.loreSource: world/sources/catalogue/type-recipes.json hist-village (3-8 villagers; one elevated member on the tree-minder's platform); world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md M3 band 12-35 with guests; UESP Lore:Hist, Lore:Argonian for the tree-minder, the naheesh and the uxith
value.why: Eight resident villagers in five households take the recipe's top band, because the village is rich on rent: the tree-minder and the watcher, the naheesh, the pitch-taker's household and two tribe families. The M3 band is reached only in the convocation month, when up to twelve guests fill the four rented huts and the two pitches. Fourteen structures: nine huts and a round house, the arch, the minder's deck, two shelters and a rack.

spec.value: The assembly designated this Hist for tapping and issued a licence against it, for a single stage on the tree for one season. The stage stands where the crew could raise it without cutting into the root flare.
A tapper and two crew whose licence is their livelihood. They keep the stage correct and police poachers themselves, because a district that cannot police itself loses its licences.

The licence is renewed annually and the objection comes most reliably from the tribe whose tree carried the stage last year. The lay-by is out of sight of the camp and out of earshot. Night landings there are not the crew's work.

A firm terrace at 30.7 to 31.4 m under a closed canopy, rising to the hut pad at 32.7 m, with the road 526 m to the south-west. The water is not here. The reach below the camp falls 29 m in 460 m and stands in pockets. The canoe lies 370 m away at the head of the tide, where the surface runs dead level and the dredged creek carries 0.84 m for 358 m to the coast.
A licence revoked would empty the stage within a season and leave the lay-by to whoever poles up to it.

value.loreSource: type recipe sap-tapping-camp (population 2–5, an elevated member on the stage, a mule line); Lore:Hist Sap; world/sources/lore/topics/hist-placement.md §75 (a licence runs against the tree, for one season)
value.why: A licence is one stage on one tree for one season. One stage needs a tapper on the deck and two hands on the ground. Three people share a hut, keep a mule line and fill a cart. Three things are BUILT here — the stage, its stair and the hut — and the mule line, the cart and the licence board are the dressing that says what the three are for (97 C5b).

spec.value: Rebuilt after the Slaughter of 4E 48 on the best natural harbour of the south coast, smaller and lower than the city it replaced.
A reconstituted merchant council governs by tariff; it will not appoint a ruler. The last party that had one killed the city.
Hostile to the An-Xileel successor state and indispensable to a bay that must trade somewhere. It is also built over its own mass grave.

A firm crest above a shallow shelf: the stilt quarters step down from the crest to a tidal flat and a lighter quay. Big hulls anchor out on the 10 m plateau and their cargo comes ashore by lighter. The lightering is the city’s living.
If the third Hist ever spoke to one faction alone, every institution here would break at once. The rules forbid it.

value.loreSource: settlement-register.md §2 (M5, rebuilt smaller); lilmoth.md owner decision 2026-08-24 (smaller, lower, over a mass grave); 95-build-sequence.md (M5 quest band 35–60); Morrowind:Balmora as the ratio check at about 40 buildings.
value.why: Twenty-six households in bamboo huts and the tall block, at five to a household, give about 130 residents; the council, the patrol, the tenders, the licence and salvage staff and the lighter crews housed on the quay add 60 to 100 more. Fifty-three placed structures is a third more than Balmora’s forty, which is the right size for a major city rebuilt smaller than the one that it replaced. Seventy named residents follows Morrowind’s ratio of named people to buildings.

spec.value: An adult wamasu grew into a small perched pan of standing water west of the zone's poling creeks and has held it for years.
The animal holds ground that it can charge; the villages have stopped trying to take it back and leave offerings on the south bank in the old Shadowfen manner.
Boats keep to the pole-marked creek below the pond rather than the shorter line past it; the detour costs two hours and the pole line needs patching every season.

The one closed body of still water within 300 m: fed by the water table, cut off from the tidal creeks, some ten metres above the creek that carries them and shallow enough that the animal can stand in all of it. A low bank ring, a knoll above the north-west shore and a cave mouth at the west waterline that floods to the roof.
Killing the animal reopens the direct line and ends the offerings; the tribes disagree about whether that is a gain.

value.loreSource: type-recipes.json#wamasu-pond (slots.population: one to three wamasu; the elevated member is a hunter's abandoned stand; countBand 4-7 lairs of this type), Lore:Wamasu, Lore:Haynekhtnamet.
value.why: A beast lair is sized by its creature count and its structure count, not by households: the adult variant of the recipe carries a single resident animal. Its two structures are the abandoned hunter's stand named in the recipe and the offering platform that Lore:Haynekhtnamet licenses. No dwelling, no door, no resident people. The count is two. The stand's footing and its deck are one structure in two stacked pieces, so the validator counts the structure and not its parts.

knownRedWarnings.why: 57/57 natural-flood-band samples but 0/57 open-water and 0/57 wet-season samples: two water layers disagreeing about the same ground, not a placement defect. The water handoff is explicit that this is water-owned - 'Preserve the authored ring and require final raised-pad evidence; do not move or relabel the huts to silence the finding.' Dry ground 8-12 m away was tested and every candidate breaks door-on-way, a fence crossing, or the 16/ha density cap.

Same layer disagreement as guest-hut-1: 57/57 flood-band, 0/57 open-water, 0/57 wet-season. This hut is also the physical host of the quest record 'The empty hut of Water Without Ceremony: the absent tribe's place', so it is not a candidate for cutting.

Not a placement defect and not a water finding: the mule trough and tie line samples 0 open-water, 0 flood-band and 0 wet-season, and so does every other parcel here. The rule asks every `work` parcel to touch water, which is written for quays. This is a licensed tapping camp on a jungle terrace at 30.7-32.7 m; its own siting record measures the nearest water a canoe can leave by at 370 m away, and the landing is a separate berth at the head of the tide. The camp cannot satisfy a quay rule and should not: the same rule-scope defect as the two Lilmoth rows above.

Not a placement defect and not a water finding: the tapping stage itself samples 0 open-water, 0 flood-band and 0 wet-season, and so does every other parcel here. The rule asks every `work` parcel to touch water, which is written for quays. This is a licensed tapping camp on a jungle terrace at 30.7-32.7 m; its own siting record measures the nearest water a canoe can leave by at 370 m away, and the landing is a separate berth at the head of the tide. The camp cannot satisfy a quay rule and should not: the same rule-scope defect as the two Lilmoth rows above.

Not a placement defect and not a water finding: the stage deck it carries samples 0 open-water, 0 flood-band and 0 wet-season, and so does every other parcel here. The rule asks every `work` parcel to touch water, which is written for quays. This is a licensed tapping camp on a jungle terrace at 30.7-32.7 m; its own siting record measures the nearest water a canoe can leave by at 370 m away, and the landing is a separate berth at the head of the tide. The camp cannot satisfy a quay rule and should not: the same rule-scope defect as the two Lilmoth rows above.

Not a placement defect and not a water finding: the stair up to that deck samples 0 open-water, 0 flood-band and 0 wet-season, and so does every other parcel here. The rule asks every `work` parcel to touch water, which is written for quays. This is a licensed tapping camp on a jungle terrace at 30.7-32.7 m; its own siting record measures the nearest water a canoe can leave by at 370 m away, and the landing is a separate berth at the head of the tide. The camp cannot satisfy a quay rule and should not: the same rule-scope defect as the two Lilmoth rows above.

Not a water finding: the crown's buildings are genuinely dry (0 open-water, 0 flood, 0 wet-season on six of seven). The district's own record puts it on the 11-13 m bench east of the crest, so 15-30% of it can never stand over water; the defect is the culture rule's scope, applied to every argonian-stilt district regardless of the ground it stands on. Fixing that is a rule design decision, queued rather than taken here.

All seven fishers' huts stand in the mapped flood band (7-42 of ~41 samples each, three of them wet-season inundated) yet the open-water layer reports 0 for every one of them. The estuary flat the record describes is wet; the open-water raster does not yet agree with the flood and wet-season fields. Same layer disagreement as the Nine-Trunks huts.
